disk_network_ultra_min.description: Minimum size of network volume allowed per node for this cluster type, expressed in gigabytes (GB). The requested disk size must be greater than or equal to network_ultra_min and satisfy any disk-to-vCPU ratio.

disk_vcpus_multiplier.description:
Disk-to-vCPU ratio (in GB per vCPU). The requested disk must be at least `vcpus` * `disk_vcpus_multiplier` GB.
Example: multiplier 32 ⇒ 1 vCPU → 32 GB, 2 vCPU → 64 GB, etc.

ram_max.description: Maximum RAM allowed per node, in MB.

ram_min.description: Minimum RAM allowed per node, in MB.

ram_vcpus_multiplier.description:
RAM-to-vCPU ratio (in GB per vCPU). The requested RAM must be at least `vCPUs` * `ram_vcpus_multiplier` GB.
Example: multiplier 4 ⇒ 1 vCPU → 4 GB, 2 vCPU → 8 GiB, etc.

vcpus_max.description: Maximum number of vCPUs allowed per node for this cluster type.

vcpus_min.description: Minimum number of vCPUs allowed per node for this cluster type.

vcpus_multiplier_min_threshold.description:
vCPU count threshold (inclusive) below which the multipliers do not apply. If `vcpus` ≤ `vcpus_multiplier_min_threshold`, both `ram_vcpus_multiplier` and `disk_vcpus_multiplier` are ignored; if `vcpus` > `vcpus_multiplier_min_threshold`, enforce RAM ≥ `vcpus` * `ram_vcpus_multiplier` and disk ≥ `vcpus` * `disk_vcpus_multiplier`.
Example: `vcpus_multiplier_min_threshold` = 8 → at vCPUs <= 8 multipliers are off; at 9 vCPUs they apply.

vcpus_steps.description: The step size for vCPU allocation. The requested number of vCPUs must be a multiple of this value. Example: if `vcpus_step` = 4, valid values are 4, 8, 12, etc.

tags.description: Access control lists (ACLs) in a Kafka cluster define actions on topics, consumer groups, and the cluster that users can perform. Use these endpoints to grant or restrict permissions by pattern and scope.
tags.name: Access Control Lists

tags.description: Information on actions performed in a cluster, used to track status, timing, and context of changes.
tags.name: Actions

tags.description: Available extensions that can be used to extend the functionality of a database within a cluster.
tags.name: Available extensions

tags.description: The set of capabilities available in the region, grouped by feature type. Each capability indicates whether a feature is supported.
tags.name: Capabilities

tags.description: Configuration parameters are tunable settings of a cluster that can be changed to adjust its behavior, performance, and security.
tags.name: Configuration parameters

tags.description: Managing databases within a cluster. Use these endpoints for CRUD operations and to inspect their metadata and status.
tags.name: Databases

tags.description: Managing clusters. Provides endpoints for CRUD operations and for performing operational actions such as rotating passwords, fetching logs/metrics, adjusting configuration, scaling, and toggling protection mode.
tags.name: Clusters

tags.description: Available database engines that can be used to create a cluster (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.).
tags.name: Cluster types

tags.description: Managing database extensions — optional features/plugins enabled per database. Provides endpoints to list used extensions, enable or disable them for a database, and inspect their version and status.
tags.name: Extensions

tags.description: Predefined compute configurations (vCPU, RAM, disk) used for cluster nodes. Provides endpoints to list available flavors, view details for specific flavor.
tags.name: Flavors

tags.description: Managing Floating IPs — externally routable addresses assignable to a node port for public access. Provides endpoints to associate or dissociate them with clusters.
tags.name: Floating ips

tags.description: Managing privileges assigned to users/roles on a database. Provides endpoints to grant or revoke permissions and to inspect current user access.
tags.name: Grants

tags.description: Platform limits for cluster configuration, including per-cluster-type min/max bounds (vCPU, RAM, local disk) and multiplier rules.
tags.name: Limits

tags.description:
Managing logical replication slots for PostgreSQL clusters. Provides endpoints to create, list, and drop slots, and to inspect status/current activity. 

Slots retain WAL until consumed — use with care to avoid disk growth.
tags.name: Logical replication slots

tags.description: Managing Prometheus metrics access tokens for customer managed monitoring. Provides endpoints to issue and revoke tokens, and to view list or specific token.
tags.name: Prometheus metrics tokens

tags.description: Quotas are per-project resource limits used to control consumption and limit costs (e.g., clusters, vCPU, RAM, storage, etc.).
tags.name: Quotas

tags.description: Managing database users within a cluster. Provides endpoints to create, retrieve, update, and delete users, rotate passwords.
tags.name: Users

tags.description: Managing Kafka topics — the logical streams of records. Provides endpoints to create, list, update, and delete topics.
tags.name: Topics
